content: Verified Jellyfin binding/API findings (2026-10-05): The bundled Jellyfin OpenAPI 10.11.6 spec already defines GET /UserImage with query parameters userId (UUID), tag, and format, and an image/* binary response. The checked-in generated ImageApi.getUserImage(UUID, String, ImageFormat) method returns a downloaded File, so regeneration is not needed to call this endpoint. Jellyfin's latest stable OpenAPI (12.1.0 at verification time, served from https://repo.jellyfin.org/releases/openapi/jellyfin-openapi-stable.json) contains the same operation and parameters. Upstream's path-based GET /Users/{userId}/Images/{imageType} is a legacy route explicitly marked Obsolete and ApiExplorerSettings(IgnoreApi = true), so don't use it for generated-client integration. The live Jellyfin 12.1.0 server returned 200 image/jpeg for GET /UserImage?userId=...&tag=...&format=Jpg both anonymously and with X-Emby-Token. GET /UserImage does not define maxWidth/maxHeight; don't send them. No account identifiers, profile data, or API credentials are retained here.
title: Jellyfin OpenAPI User Image Route

Procedure: Use a 5.3-or-later runtime only. The previous openhab-development-server container used openhab/openhab:5.2.3-debian and exited with code 137 on 2026-11-03; do not reuse it for migrated code. The replacement image last verified locally on 2026-11-03 is openhab/openhab:snapshot-debian, image label version 5.3.0-snapshot, Java 21.0.11, registry digest openhab/openhab@sha256:0b6782ed409150c3ec89c4f3656b4fbf1dedd08db98bb4038cc0f22408ca99ef. On another workstation run `docker pull openhab/openhab:snapshot-debian`, inspect `org.opencontainers.image.version` and `org.opencontainers.image.revision`, and run `docker run --rm --entrypoint java openhab/openhab:snapshot-debian -version`. The snapshot tag is mutable; use the recorded digest only to reproduce the exact image observed on 2026-11-03, and use a current image labeled 5.3 or later for acceptance. Create or verify a dedicated test container with machine-appropriate isolated configuration mounts; do not assume the previous name, host paths, bridge setup, or bundle IDs are portable. Build the binding JAR, copy only the main JAR into the watched `/openhab/addons` directory, verify its SHA-256 inside the container, then use an authenticated interactive openHAB console to inspect the actual bundle and Things. Protect credentials and account identities; do not put tokens in chat or artifacts. Verify identity channels with linked Items only after metadata and implementation tasks are complete.

The historical 5.2.3 runtime passed baseline smoke checks before the status API migration and is not compatible acceptance evidence.
Rollback: For a newly added candidate, remove only that JAR from the watched add-ons directory. For an update, restore the backed-up JAR. Never delete persistent configuration or userdata. Do not force OSGi resolution or weaken imports if the bundle is incompatible.
